chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
If a man kills a woman and the family of the woman intend to kill him (in retaliation), they should pay half the blood money (diyah) to the family of the man.

key_terms.أَحَدُهُمَا: One of the two (referring to the 5th or 6th Imam)
key_terms.الدِّيَة: Blood money or compensation paid for killing or injury

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Qisas when a man kills a woman and her family seeks to kill him in return?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of 'Damm al-Mukhallas' (mixed blood money), establishing that when a man kills a woman, the female heirs retain the right to exact Qisas (retaliation) by killing the murderer, provided they compensate the male heirs for the difference in Diyah. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the gender of the victim does not preclude the right to life-for-life retribution, but rather adjusts the financial compensation due to the unequal distribution of inheritance shares between male and female relatives.
